title: Why Christians read the Torah
hookLine: Jesus quoted Deuteronomy in the desert and summed the law in two commandments from it

lines: FIVE WEEKS IN THE BOOKS OF MOSES.
cards: Plagues and Passover. Manna and mountains. For five weeks now, this path has walked through Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy.
A fair question, on a Christian path: why? Most churches don't keep the food laws, and none offer animal sacrifices. Here's one place to start.
When Jesus was alone in the desert, hungry and tempted three times, he answered three times. And every answer was a quotation from one book. Deuteronomy.

teach.b: Torah is usually translated law, but it's closer to teaching, or instruction: the way a parent points a child down the right road. It's the Jewish name for the first five books of the Bible, the books of Moses.
For Jesus, these were scripture; he grew up hearing them read in the synagogue.
In the desert he answered the tempter with them: man shall not live by bread alone; thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God; worship God and serve him only.
Near the end of his life, someone asks him which commandment is the greatest, and he reaches into the Torah twice.

In Matthew's Gospel, in the King James Bible: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets."
The first comes from the Shema in Deuteronomy, the line right after hear, O Israel. The second is from Leviticus.
Hang: like a door on its two hinges, everything else swings on these two.

teach.h: NOT TO DESTROY, BUT TO FULFIL.
teach.b: Jesus also said, "Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil." Christians have understood that in different ways.
Catholic, Orthodox and many Protestant teachers distinguish the moral law, which still guides, from ceremonial laws they see as fulfilled in Christ.
Lutherans often speak of law and gospel, the law showing our need and the gospel meeting it.

teach.h: ON THESE TWO COMMANDMENTS HANG ALL THE LAW.
teach.b: But nearly all of them read these books as their own scripture, shared with the Jewish people, who read them first.

how: Most churches read from the Old Testament, including the Torah, in worship, and many Christians learn Jesus' summary of the law, the two great commandments, by heart.

games.q: you're Jesus. someone asks: which commandment is the greatest? where do you go for the answer?
o: a new commandment of your own.
the first of the ten words only.
games.why: he quotes Deuteronomy (love God) and Leviticus (love thy neighbour): on these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

practice: Hold the two hinges. On one breath, call the first to mind: love God with all your heart and soul and mind; on the next, the second: love your neighbor as yourself.
Notice which one feels closer to your life today, and if you pray, ask for help with the harder one.
